flawed_step: Step 2: Inferring that the edge condition forces all vertices into one component, and hence toward one common triangle vertex, is unjustified. Step 1—the observation that each connected component separately inherits the edge condition—is valid, but the hypothesis imposes no relation between distinct components.
counterexample: Let V={1,2,3,4,5,6} and E={{1,2},{2,3},{3,1},{4,5},{5,6},{6,4}}: the disjoint union of two triangles. Its only triangles are {1,2,3} and {4,5,6}, so every edge lies in exactly one triangle. Every vertex has degree 2, whereas a universal vertex would have degree 5. Thus there is no vertex adjacent to all the others.
assessment_summary: The claim is false because its hypothesis is componentwise and the graph is explicitly not assumed connected. Two disjoint triangles satisfy the exact-one-triangle condition but have no universal vertex.
